programs.title: Prince of Persia
programs.subtitle: Apple II, 1989
programs.author: Jordan Mechner
programs.description: The game that invented cinematic platformers — built by one developer over four years on Apple II hardware with 128K of RAM. The source code was recovered in 2012 from 22-year-old floppy disks.

files.title: SOUND.S
files.description: The complete sound engine — twenty sounds, one speaker, zero compromises

files.title: BOOT.S
files.description: The two-stage disk boot loader with 128K memory check

files.title: SEQTABLE.S
files.description: The animation state machine — every movement rotoscoped from film

files.title: MASTER.S
files.description: Game flow controller: boot, attract mode, save/load, level sequencing

programs.title: Zork
programs.subtitle: PDP-10 / ITS, 1977–1979
programs.author: Anderson, Blank, Daniels, Lebling
programs.description: The game that invented the text adventure — built organically at MIT on a PDP-10, recovered from a 1990 tape, and released open-source in 2025. Its parser, its puzzles, and its sarcastic error messages changed computing forever.

files.title: defs.63
files.description: The complete type system — ROOM, OBJECT, SYNTAX, and the parser data structures

files.title: np.93
files.description: The 93rd version of the natural language parser

files.title: dung.56
files.description: The world itself — every room, exit, and object in the dungeon

files.title: act1.38
files.description: Game loop, action handlers, and the real access-control guard

programs.title: MS-DOS
programs.subtitle: IBM PC, 1981–1983
programs.author: Tim Paterson / Microsoft
programs.description: Written in six weeks by one programmer, acquired by Microsoft for $25,000, and licensed to IBM — then to every IBM clone maker on earth. The source code of the PC era.

files.title: MSDOS.ASM
files.description: The original 86-DOS kernel — Tim Paterson's byline and a revision history written in assembly comments

files.title: COMMAND.ASM
files.description: The command interpreter — 'Abort, Retry, Ignore?' in its original form

files.title: XENIX.ASM
files.description: The Unix layer that gave DOS subdirectories, pipes, and file handles

files.title: MSCODE.ASM
files.description: The v2.0 kernel — the INT 21h dispatcher and a comment that says 'Here comes multitasking!!!'
